_readme: The Skill power/cost curve, one row per character level. Every character's Skill action automatically uses whichever tier matches their current level (see FightController.SpellTierFor) — there's no separate spell-picking UI, this is what makes Skill get stronger and costlier as a character levels 1-9. Every field is required (no auto-defaulting, unlike enemies.json) since a progression table is exactly the kind of content that deserves a deliberately hand-picked number at every step. Level 1's numbers (manaCost 10, powerMultiplier 1.5) match what every character's Skill always cost/dealt before this system existed, so a level-1 character is unaffected. scalesWith is optional and holds '<ability score> <grade>' lines (S, A, B, C, D, E, or none): it multiplies ALONGSIDE powerMultiplier, riding the caster's own scores rather than the weapon in their hand, so a Strength build swings hard and casts weakly and an Intelligence build the reverse. Ten is the neutral score — a tier with no scalesWith, or a caster sitting at ten, multiplies by exactly 1.0 and behaves as it did before scaling existed. The curve below deepens with level on purpose: a level-1 Spark barely cares who is casting it, an Ascendance cares enormously, so investing in Intelligence pays off later rather than immediately.
